source.title: The neuroscience of empathy: progress, pitfalls and promise.

confidence_rationale: Authoritative review separating two empathic sub-processes, experience sharing and explicit mentalizing, supported by distinct neural systems. Endorses the sharing route MECH-405 describes while making clear that empathy is not reducible to it. A review rather than new data, so confidence is moderate.
failure_signatures: A two-system framing can be read as supporting either a pure-sharing mechanism or a pure-inference one; the claim should not cite it for more than the existence of a sharing route plus a separate mentalizing route.
Review notes artificial stimuli and weak brain-behaviour links in the underlying studies, so the sharing evidence it summarises inherits those limits.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Empathy comprises at least two sub-processes, sharing others' internal states and explicitly considering those states, supported by separable neural systems; much early research used artificial stimuli and lacked links between brain activity and social behaviour.
mapping.ree_translation: Maps MECH-405 onto the 'experience sharing' sub-process only. The mentalizing sub-process corresponds to the other-model (ARC-083/OBJ-5) doing more than hold a binding slot: it computes the other's state. The claim should say which sub-process 'fast empathy' names.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Conceptual review; the 'fast' label in MECH-405 plausibly maps to sharing, but the review does not measure speed and does not claim sharing is sufficient for concern or prosocial action.
mapping.source_context: Nature Neuroscience perspective/review of a decade of empathy neuroscience.

confidence_components.notes: Well-cited review, no new data; useful mainly for scoping the claim.
